Long, long ago, there lived a prophet named Jonah. One day he was given an important task: “Go to the great city of Nineveh and tell its people they must not live this way any longer — let them change their ways.” Jonah listened… and fell into deep thought.

But Jonah didn't want to go to Nineveh at all: the city was huge, the people were angry — how scary! So he came up with a "clever" plan: to sail away on a ship in the other direction, as far away as he could. As if you could ever run away from something important!

A ship happened to be in the harbor, all set to sail far, far away—to Tarshish. Jonah paid for his passage, climbed aboard, and hid down below in the hold. The ship set sail, and the runaway... fell fast asleep, calm as could be.

Suddenly a terrible storm rose up! The waves tossed the ship about like a tiny chip of wood, and the wind tore at the sails. The sailors threw the cargo overboard to make the ship lighter, shouting to each other over the howling wind. But Jonah just kept sleeping down in the hold — fast, fast asleep.

The sailors woke Jonah: “Who’s to blame for this storm?!” And then Jonah told the truth: “It’s me. I’m running away from an important task. Throw me into the sea — and the storm will stop.” The sailors didn’t want to, but the waves kept rising higher and higher…

The moment Jonah hit the water, the storm calmed and the sea grew smooth. Then, from the deep, up rose a huge, enormous fish — and swallowed Jonah whole, like a little berry. The sailors gasped. But this wasn't the end of the story — it was only the middle.

Inside the fish, it was a bit dark, a bit cramped, and very quiet — like the strangest room in the whole world. But at least nothing could stop him from thinking. And Jonah had plenty to think about: turns out, you can't sail away from a task, not even to the edge of the sea.

For three days and three nights, Jonah thought it over — about how he'd been afraid, about how he'd run away, and about how a job you're given will always be waiting for you. "If I get out of here," Jonah decided, "I'll go to Nineveh. I promise!"

And then the fish swam up to the shore and — splash! — gently set Jonah down on the warm sand. Wet, ruffled, but alive and safe! “Thank you,” said Jonah to the fish. This was his second chance, and he wasn’t about to waste it.

Nineveh really was enormous: to walk it from end to end took three whole days! The gates were like mountains, the streets like rivers. Once, Jonah would have been scared. But now he took a deep breath — and walked into the city.

In the biggest square, Jonah gathered his courage and told the truth: "People of Nineveh! You can't go on like this — you cheat and hurt one another. If you don't change your ways, trouble will come!" He said it — then squeezed his eyes shut, sure they'd chase him away...

But then a miracle happened: everyone listened to him! Everyone — from the simplest shepherd to the king himself. People began to make peace, return what wasn't theirs, and help one another. A whole great city decided to become kinder — and so it did!

Nothing bad happened to the city — and you know what? Jonah… got upset! He sat down on a hill outside the city and pouted: “I walked so far, I gave them warning, and yet nothing bad happened. So it was all for nothing?” What a grumbler he was!

In the night, a wonder-plant grew up beside Jonah — tall, with big leaves like burdock. In the morning, it shaded the old grumbler from the hot sun, like a green umbrella. “Now that's what I call caring!” Jonah beamed, and for the first time that day, he smiled.

But the next day, the plant withered. And Jonah felt so sorry for it — he almost cried! "My poor little tree," he sighed, "you had only just grown..." So the prophet sat on the hill, crying over the withered plant.

Then Jonah heard a quiet question: “Do you feel sorry for a plant you never grew? But in Nineveh there are thousands of people and children, and they all needed a chance to change. How could I not feel sorry for them?” And at last, Jonah understood everything.

And that's the story of a prophet who tried to run away. Everyone needs a second chance sometimes: a big city, a grumpy prophet, and even you and me. The important thing is to turn around and head the right way — at just the right time!
